title: Quantum codes are quantized codes: Stabilizer codes from quantization over finite fields
abstract: We present a discrete analogue of geometric quantization over finite fields which, when applied to certain classical error-correcting codes, yields quantum error-correcting codes. This provides a physical interpretation for a previously known quantum-classical correspondence in coding theory.
summary: This paper constructs a discrete analogue of geometric quantization applicable to finite fields. It shows that quantum error-correcting codes can be understood as the quantization of classical constraints defined on a symplectic vector space. This establishes a rigorous, physical interpretation for the mathematical relationship between classical coding theory and quantum stabilizer codes.
main_problem: To develop a discrete analogue of geometric quantization over finite fields, providing a physical interpretation for the correspondence between classical and quantum error-correcting codes.
main_result: The quantization procedure successfully maps classical constraints (defined by isotropic subspaces in a symplectic vector space over $\mathbb{F}_d$) to quantum stabilizer constraints, demonstrating that quantum codes are fundamentally quantized codes.
method: The authors adapt geometric quantization techniques, originally for continuous symplectic manifolds, to the discrete setting of finite fields using displacement operators and polarization analogues.
model_or_system: The model involves symplectic vector spaces $(V, \omega)$ over finite fields $\mathbb{F}_d$, relating classical linear codes (defined by constraints) to quantum stabilizer codes on $d$-dimensional qudits.
key_observables: Stabilizer constraints, logical Pauli operators, and the resulting code space dimension $[[n, k]]_d$.
important_parameters: The dimension $d$ of the qudit (often an odd prime), and the structure of the symplectic form $\omega$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on establishing a discrete analogue of the Segal-Bargmann representation and assuming the compatibility of quantization with symplectic reduction.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first reviewing continuous geometric quantization, then developing the discrete analogue over finite fields, and finally applying this framework to explicitly derive the structure of stabilizer codes from classical coding theory constraints.
why_interesting: It provides a deep mathematical link between abstract algebraic structures (symplectic geometry over finite fields) and the physical realization of quantum error correction codes, which is foundational to quantum computation theory.
